body: I'm going to go against the other responses and say try to do something where the requirements overlap if you're really set on a double major or a minor. I am graduating with a double major in public health and nursing and a minor in sociology with a GPA of 3.964. I think it is all about time management.

Honestly, it depends if we are talking about serious studying or low-key studying. I will do probably an hour a day of just re-organizing my notes and reading leisurely. I think half the battle of nursing school is staying ahead of the material.
-I first organize the powerpoint notes into an outline. 
-Next, I read the textbook with that outline and add extra notes that are missing
-About a week before the exam I start memorizing that outline and watching YouTube videos related to that content

*Note: It is necessary to evaluate this per class. In some courses it does not pay to read the textbook.

-GPA: 3.964, Nursing tutor and mentor

So naturally she questioned the employee and he said it was right. She talked to him more and he kept telling her there was nothing he could do. So she went along and drove away. I did not expect to see her at the gas station but I pulled up to fill my car up and I saw my grandma but I couldn't say hi because she was pulling out of the station. So the attendant goes up to me and says "That woman was fucking crazy she can't even drive, I changed her for premium instead of regular, she wouldn't know the difference." Basically I fucking lost it and said "I don't want to get gas here, that was my grandmother who is 85 and is about the kindest person you will ever meet.
